sovereign_country.strategic_role: 非洲第一大金融枢纽、辐射南部非洲关税同盟（SACU）商贸

business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Time-Definite Small Parcel Courier Operations

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Africa (national level; unitary - no sub-state tax distinction for company incorporation)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Roman-Dutch common law with English common law influence, constitutional supremacy)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Protection of Investment Act 22 of 2015 (domestic investment-protection framework; most pre-2015 bilateral investment treaties terminated)
SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment (2006)
South Africa–United States Double Taxation Agreement (1997, as amended)
South Africa–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (2002, as amended)
South Africa–People's Republic of China Double Taxation Agreement (2000)
WTO GATS commitments on courier services (CPC 7512)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, covering s1 definitions, s13 power to incorporate, s14 registration and certificate, s19 legal personality, s66 board of directors, and s69 directors; together with the Companies Regulations, 2011, including prescribed Forms CoR 14.1 and CoR 14.1B.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), operating under the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic), South Africa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CIPC Form CoR 14.1), filed together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) via CIPC eServices.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is imposed under the Companies Act 71 of 2008, and no escrow or blocked capital account is required. Shares may be issued for cash, property, or services as approved by the board; any unpaid or deferred payment arrangement must be recorded in the share register and board minutes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IT IS RESOLVED at the first quorate board meeting of [Company Name] (Pty) Ltd held on [date], that: (1) the issue of 100 ordinary shares to the initial subscriber is ratified, and the subscription consideration is approved; (2) the principal premises named in the Notice of Incorporation are adopted as the registered office and legal service address; (3) [Name] is appointed sole director and [Name] company secretary, with immediate effect; and (4) the public officer and all authorised signatories are empowered to execute SARS, CIPC, CBRTA, ICASA and banking applications required to commence courier operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the proposed company name with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an applicant profile on CIPC eServices or BizPortal using a certified South African ID, smart ID, or foreign passport. File an online name reservation application specifying the preferred name and two alternative names, together with required search terms. Pay the applicable name reservation fee by debit/credit card or electronic transfer. CIPC performs automated and manual screening, and issues a name reservation certificate valid for 60 days upon approval.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of applicant’s South African ID, smart ID, or passport
Power of attorney or accredited agent agreement if filing through a service provider
Completed name reservation application with first and alternative names
Proof of proposed registered office address
Payment reference for the CIPC name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, review the written CIPC reason, refile with fresh alternatives before the 60-day reservation window expires, or lodge a name dispute and hearing request under section 160 of the Companies Act with CIPC for a formal remedy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company legal adviser, notary public, or commissioner of oaths in South Africa; notarisation or apostille for signatures executed abroad
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI to include the company’s name, registered office, authorised shares, share classes, board composition, director powers, quorum, and any lawful variation of the Companies Act default provisions. Complete Form CoR 14.1 and the director consent forms. Have the incorporator, each director, and the company secretary, where appointed, sign before a commissioner of oaths. If executed outside South Africa, legalise or apostille the signatures before submission.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum of Incorporation
Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1)
Consent to act as director forms (Form CoR 14.1B or equivalent)
Certified identification copies of incorporator, directors, and secretary
Proof of registered office premises and owner’s/landlord’s consent to use the address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC identifies defective execution or incomplete MOI schedules, correct the affected signature or schedule and resubmit through the online filing queue; if the MOI is invalid after registration, a special resolution may cure the defect under section 16 of the Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit incorporation documents to CIPC and pay the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC eServices electronic filing system; accredited CIPC agents may be used
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the completed and signed CoR 14.1, MOI, director consent forms, identity documents, and name reservation certificate to CIPC eServices. Verify the prescribed fee according to the current CIPC fee schedule, make the online payment, and submit the application for adjudication. CIPC will allocate a company registration number and, upon satisfaction of formalities, issue a Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1)
Signed Memorandum of Incorporation
Director consent forms and certified ID/passport copies
Name reservation certificate
Proof of payment of CIPC registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC raises a requisition, respond within the stated deadline, typically 15 business days, via the CIPC online portal by correcting the defect and, where required, paying a resubmission fee. If the registration is erroneously refused, apply to the CIPC Registration Committee for reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and establish statutory corporate records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Certificate of Incorporation from CIPC eServices immediately after approval and verify the company name, registration number, and date of registration. Open and maintain the company’s statutory records: share register, register of directors, register of company secretary, accounting officer appointment, and beneficial ownership register. Record the initial share allotment and file the beneficial ownership information with CIPC within the prescribed statutory period.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation
Date-stamped Notice of Incorporation
Registered Memorandum of Incorporation
Share subscription and allotment listing
Beneficial ownership declarations and director declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is withheld pending beneficial ownership data, co-ordinate with the directors and beneficial owners to file the prescribed declaration. If CIPC has made a clerical error in the certificate, request an administrative correction through the CIPC contact procedure or Form CoR 14.14.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with SARS, appoint the public officer, and open corporate bank accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling and branch offices; banking institution subject to FICA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax with SARS, obtain an income tax reference number, and register for VAT, PAYE, and UIF where applicable. Appoint a public officer as required under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 and notify SARS. Open a corporate bank account using the Certificate of Incorporation, MOI, and FICA documents; complete the bank’s customer due diligence and beneficial ownership verification for the express courier business payments.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum of Incorporation
SARS business registration application and supporting turnover/VAT threshold evidence
Public officer appointment resolution or tax registration declaration
Certified ID/passport copies and proof of residential address for directors and beneficial owners
Bank account forms and FICA declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS queries the tax registration or public officer appointment, resubmit a corrected business registration via eFiling, provide a certified board resolution confirming the public officer, and obtain a SARS Notice of Registration before commencing operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Independent Communications Authority of South Africa (ICASA) for the postal/courier service licence; Cross-Border Road Transport Agency (CBRTA) for cross-border road transport permits; South African Revenue Service Customs under the Customs and Excise Act 91 of 1964 for import/export formalities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Individual Postal Service Licence for Express/Courier Services under the Postal Services Act 124 of 1998, as amended, together with any required road carrier permit and customs registration for international courier operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) under the National Environmental Management Act 107 of 1998, with delegated provincial environmental authorities where applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: An ordinary small-parcel courier depot is generally exempt from a full EIA where it meets zoning and local authority bylaws. A Basic Assessment or EIA Registration under Listing Notice 1 of the EIA Regulations, 2014, is triggered if the depot exceeds 2,000 m², involves significant groundwater abstraction, or is located in an environmentally sensitive area. A full EIA under Listing Notice 2 is required only for scheduled large infrastructure, hazardous waste storage, or developments within protected and conservation areas.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater and trade effluent discharges must comply with section 68 of the National Water Act 36 of 1998, any applicable water use licence, and municipal sewer bylaws. Atmospheric emissions from standby generators or motor vehicle facilities must meet the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 licensing thresholds and minimum emission standards where applicable. Waste handling must be performed by registered waste transporters and disposed of at licensed landfill sites under the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the applicable municipal fire department, compliance with Part T of the National Building Regulations (SANS 10400) and the Fire Brigade Services Act; structural load inspection and certificate from a registered professional engineer confirming the warehouse floor and racking capacity; and occupational clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993, including electrical installation certificate, hazardous chemical agent assessment where relevant, Compensation Fund letter of good standing, and workplace compliance inspection.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); taxpayer portal: SARS eFiling (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za); customs and excise division: SARS Customs via SAD500/EDI (https://www.sars.gov.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned South African (Pty) Ltd, SARS registration is separate from CIPC incorporation. Steps: (1) incorporate the company with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) and obtain the CIPC company registration certificate; (2) register the company on SARS eFiling as an income-tax taxpayer, using the CIPC registration details, and obtain a SARS income tax reference number; (3) if the value of taxable supplies exceeds R1,000,000 in any rolling 12-month period, submit SARS form VAT101 (Application for Registration as a VAT Vendor), or apply voluntarily once taxable supplies exceed R50,000; (4) if the entity is a non-resident external company, register as an external company with CIPC, register with SARS for income tax on South African-source income, and appoint a local representative taxpayer; (5) for VAT, a non-resident carrying on an enterprise through a representative vendor in South Africa must appoint that representative vendor to act for it; (6) submit the required eFiling records: CIPC registration certificate, Memorandum of Incorporation, director/shareholder identification and passport copies, registered office proof, confirmation of a South African bank account, and signed authority for any appointed representative; (7) SARS will issue the income tax reference number and, where applicable, a separate VAT vendor number through eFiling; the company must maintain a valid Tax Compliance Status (TCS) PIN for customs clearance, banking, and cross-border transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no US-style check-the-box election and no general pass-through election for a (Pty) Ltd; the company is automatically a separate entity-level taxpayer. Elections and statutory options relevant to a cross-border express courier operator include: (i) voluntary VAT registration under s.23 of the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991; (ii) VAT group registration under s.50 VAT Act for connected companies to be treated as a single vendor; (iii) micro business turnover tax election for qualifying companies with annual turnover not exceeding R1,000,000; (iv) small business corporation concessional income-tax rates, where company qualifications are satisfied; (v) CFC high-tax exemption under s.9D(2A) of the Income Tax Act; and (vi) hybrid mismatch rules, which apply automatically under the statutory anti-hybrid provisions and are not subject to elective disapplication.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration in South African Rand (ZAR) when the value of taxable supplies exceeds R1,000,000 in the preceding 12 months; voluntary registration is available once taxable supplies exceed R50,000. A non-resident supplier carrying on an enterprise in South Africa must register and may be required to appoint a South African representative vendor.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently impose real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, mandatory government pre-clearance, or digital stamping of ordinary VAT invoices. SARS eFiling is the mandatory channel for filing VAT returns, and export declarations are filed digitally as SAD500 Bills of Entry through SARS Customs EDI or Remote Processing. VAT tax invoices may be issued electronically or on paper under s.20 VAT Act, provided they include all prescribed particulars and are issued within 21 days of the supply. The SAD500 customs release, not a digital stamp, is the operative export clearance record.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A registered South African VAT vendor may zero-rate a supply of movable goods exported from South Africa under s.11(1)(a) VAT Act, and may zero-rate international transport, freight forwarding, and courier services supplied in respect of exported goods or supplied to a non-resident, provided the goods are physically removed from South Africa under a valid customs declaration and the supplier obtains and retains acceptable proof of export. The onus is on the vendor to prove entitlement. For cross-border express courier operations, the service must be separate from any domestic leg and the zero-rated consideration must be identifiable on the tax invoice. Input VAT attributable to the zero-rated supply may be deducted, and any excess credit is refundable through the VAT201 refund system. If export proof is not retained or the goods are not removed as recorded, the supply is reclassified as standard-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SARS Customs export declaration (SAD500 Bill of Entry) with customs acknowledgment or release reference
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) evidencing the physical departure of the goods from South Africa
Commercial invoice and VAT tax invoice issued under s.20 of the Value-Added Tax Act
Proof of export such as signed proof of delivery, route documents, foreign customs import evidence, or carrier release documents
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/SWIFT credit evidence showing that export proceeds were received in South Africa
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS audits export zero-rating through VAT refund reviews and the Customs Export Verification unit. Where a vendor cannot substantiate the actual export, output VAT is retrospectively clawed back to the original VAT return period, with statutory interest and penalties. The taxpayer bears the burden of proof under s.102 of the Tax Administration Act. Understatement penalties range from 20% to 200% of the assessed shortfall depending on the conduct involved, and fraudulent zero-rating may result in criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment of up to 10 years under the Tax Administration Act and the Customs and Excise Act. No prescription period applies to additional assessments when fraud or misrepresentation is proven; otherwise SARS generally has a three-year prescription window. Export documentation and all tax records must be retained for at least five years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Currency and Exchanges Act, No. 9 of 1933, as amended, and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961; day-to-day administration delegated to Authorised Dealers (Category I commercial banks) through the Electronic Monitoring and Control System (EMCS).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa is an IMF Article VIII current-account convertible regime. Current-account transactions supporting the courier business - cross-border trade settlement, carriage and freight fees, airway bill payments, agent commissions, and remittance of dividends out of genuinely realised profits - are freely convertible through an Authorised Dealer against documentary proof and SARB Balance of Payments (BOP) reporting. Capital-account flows require FinSurv authorisation unless covered by a standing general allowance; a 100% foreign-owned (Pty) Ltd is permitted, but inward equity and shareholder loans must be declared through the Authorised Dealer under the prescribed FDI notification procedure and booked under the 'N' non-resident reserve code. Profit repatriation hurdles are primarily documentary: a current SARS Tax Clearance Status/TCC is required for dividend and interest remittances, dividends are subject to 20% dividends tax at source (with treaty-based exemptions available on submission of declaration and undertaking), and the company must confirm that dividends are paid from available distributable profits audited in accordance with the Companies Act, No. 71 of 2008.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export earnings, including foreign-currency revenues for cross-border express courier services, must be fully repatriated and received by an Authorised Dealer in South Africa within 180 days of the date of export or service rendition (SAD500 or commercial invoice date). There is no mandatory minimum conversion ratio into ZAR; the exporter may retain 100% of foreign receipts in a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) with an Authorised Dealer or convert at the onshore market rate provided the funds are deployed for transactional business expenses. Compliance is monitored through the FinSurv EMCS and monthly BOP declarations; late receipt, shortfall, or unauthorised use of offshore funds must be reported via the Authorised Dealer and may trigger VAT input disallowance, penal interest, and withdrawal of the exporter's forex accommodation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for FDI injection and Multi-currency Operating Account (ZAR/USD/EUR)
Operational Account with integrated ACH Direct and Card POS acquiring plus Foreign Currency Account for export proceeds
Operational Account and Trade Finance Facility supporting Commercial Letter of Credit settlements
Operational Account with dedicated Africa trade corridor desk and ZAR/USD clearing capabilities
Corporate Tier-1 Transactional and FX Hedging Account for advanced treasury structures

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. Under the National Payment System Act, No. 78 of 1998, SARB retains exclusive authorisation over e-money issuance and settlement memberships; non-resident EMIs such as Airwallex, Wise, and Revolut Business cannot directly issue ZAR e-money, access the South African Multiple Option Settlement (SAMOS) system, or clear ACH Direct batches. Their viable role is limited to offshore collection of inbound courier fees in USD/EUR/GBP and funding of outbound partner payments outside South Africa, provided all ZAR legs settle through a licensed local bank. Any offshore balance remains subject to the 180-day repatriation rule; therefore an EMI cannot replace a Category I Authorised Dealer as the entity's principal settlement bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is technically permissible under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, No. 38 of 2001, as amended, and FIC Guidance Note 7 where the bank applies risk-based digital KYC with biometric liveness and certified document upload. In practice, for a medium-risk enhanced due diligence client with non-resident shareholders or directors, the Tier-1 banks require at least one locally resident accountable person (e.g., a South African finance director, comptroller, or attorney with power of attorney) to attend an in-person onboarding interview. A non-resident director may supplement with a video interview and apostilled corporate documents, but the prevailing expectation is personal appearance at a South African branch or verification by the bank's overseas correspondent; where no local presence exists, account activation is commonly conditioned on the appointment of a South African-based compliance officer with FICA-compliant signing powers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: non-resident shareholder or trust chain in a low-tax or blacklisted jurisdiction holding more than 25% of the (Pty) Ltd.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate structure chart; beneficial ownership register under Companies Act s.56; certified ID or passport copies of all UBOs; FATCA/CRS self-certifications; sworn source-of-funds and source-of-wealth affidavits; board resolution recording shareholding; professional reference from the group's external auditors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or negative-news exposure on courier trade lanes, including deliveries touching OFAC/UN/EU/UK-sanctioned territories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: World-Check or Refinitiv sanctions screening report for directors, customers, and consignee base; trade sanctions and export-control policy document; evidence of restricted-country blocking procedures; list of permitted consignee countries; undertaking to notify the bank 30 days in advance of any lane change.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket ACH Direct and Card POS disbursements to independent courier sub-contractors, presenting a structuring red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contractor master register with FICA-verified IDs and tax numbers; signed service-level agreements; disbursement schedules and payroll/GL extracts; maker-checker batch logic description; SARS EMP201 (PAYE) and VAT201 reconciliations; monthly bank-statement reconciliation trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Customs invoice misdeclaration in SAD500 filings for international parcels, indicating trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tariff classification worksheet per ISIC 5320 commodity group; sample commercial invoice templates with HS codes; airline airway bills and carrier manifests; time-definite courier rate card with weight-zone pricing model; customs broker licence and agency mandate; annual independent audit letter on declaration accuracy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unapproved capital-account transaction, e.g., use of offshore shareholder loan proceeds for working capital without FinSurv declaration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed loan or subscription agreement; Authorised Dealer FDI declaration/report; bank-issued non-resident 'N' code entry evidence; current-account deployment audit trail; corporate treasury and borrowing policy; legal opinion from South African exchange-control counsel confirming compliance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders inject equity or shareholder loans via SWIFT MT103 (telegraphic transfer) into the entity's Capital Escrow Account at an Authorised Dealer, using the SARB BOP purpose-of-payment code applicable to direct investment (FDI) or intercompany lending as prescribed by the Authorised Dealer's system. The remitter must cite the company's registered name and VAT registration; the Authorised Dealer completes the inward FDI declaration and assigns the 'N' non-resident reserve code within 30 days. Funds may then be converted to ZAR at the onshore market rate or credited to an FCA for operating needs; subsequent disbursement requires supporting invoices, board approval minutes, and current VAT/PAYE compliance status. For capital raising exceeding general allowance limits, the FinSurv prior approval letter must be presented before the inward remittance is credited to the account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement to foreign partner couriers, airlines, and last-mile agents is executed by SWIFT MT103 from the ZAR or FCA leg with BOP purpose codes applicable to freight and logistics services. High-value seasonal charter or capitalised freight purchases are supported by Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700) with documents against payment. Domestic subcontractors and suppliers are settled through the Automated Clearing Bureau (ACB) ACH Direct batch via SAMOS; Card POS receipts are aggregated by the acquiring bank through BankservAfrica and settled in ZAR T+1. All foreign disbursements require an Authorised Dealer-approved underlying invoice, exchange-control declaration for amounts exceeding applicable thresholds, and current SARS tax clearance to avoid payment delays.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/ZAR, EUR/ZAR, and GBP/ZAR outright forwards transacted with an Authorised Dealer under an ISDA or local master agreement, strictly limited to the courier's identified transactional trade cycle covering fuel, aircraft charters, and cross-border agent settlements.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) USD/ZAR executed offshore through a non-resident counterparty, available only where a deliverable onshore hedge is contractually or operationally impossible; a resident (Pty) Ltd is restricted by FinSurv from using NDFs without a hard underlying exposure, and any unwind must be evidenced to the Authorised Dealer.

USD/ZAR or EUR/ZAR cross-currency swap with matched principal exchange concluded through the Authorised Dealer for duration-alignment of foreign shareholder loans or bridge financing, subject to FinSurv loan approvals and annual rollover certification.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (standard company income tax rate for years of assessment ending on or after 1 April 2023; 28% for earlier years of assessment).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday regime. Relevant preferential deductions and allowances: s.11D research and development allowance (150% of qualifying R&D expenditure); s.12C accelerated wear-and-tear on plant and machinery; s.12E Small Business Corporation graduated rate schedule (0% to 27%, subject to eligibility thresholds); s.12I industrial investment allowance for qualifying greenfield and brownfield projects; s.11(e) wear-and-tear allowances for courier fleet, sorting machinery, and information technology infrastructure.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory carryforward limit (indefinite carry-forward of assessed losses under s.20 Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, subject to the continuity-of-trade and change-in-ownership limitations in s.20A).
